newsitem.title: UK: UK Takeover Panel head wants fuller disclosure.
newsitem.headline: UK Takeover Panel head wants fuller disclosure.

text.p: Alistair Defriez, director-general of Britain's Takeover Panel, said on Saturday he wanted fuller disclosure of advisers' interests but did not support a ban on financial advisers in takeovers buying shares.

"We are sending out a message to the City (of London financial district) that when advisers want to clear a course of action with the panel, they must err on the side of greater disclosure," Defriez told the Financial Times.
He was talking after the panel rebuked Barclays de Zoete Wedd for witholding information about the fees earned defending Northern Electric against a takeover.
The hostile takeover was launched by CE Electric. Northern Electric said it would make a statement in the next 48 hours or so on whether it would recommend acceptance of the 782 million pound offer.
Defriez said that if share purchases by financial advisers were banned, they would be driven underground.
"There is a risk that it would simply be done by others with an association with the target company, such as suppliers or customers who would then expect a future reward," he said.
"Our concern in the context of the Northern-CalEnergy bid is that the purchases should be at arm's length without any inducement or financial incentive from the target company."
BZW said its fees were not linked to its acquisition of Northern shares.
